Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets, CMake) with an AI agent chat. Its React AgentUI is under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`. The printer chat helps a person add and connect printers. A Bambu connection skill explains how the connection works, and the app adds it once the person tries to connect.

Kenneth wants people stuck with a problem to have a way to report it to the developers. Today there is none that works:
- After a second failed connection the chat shows a card offering to send a report, but saying yes only saves it under `<data_dir>/jusprin/connection_reports/`.
- The Help menu's "Report a bug" item is commented out.
- Links in agent messages render as plain text (`AgentUI/src/components/MarkdownMessage.tsx`).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` still points to OrcaSlicer.

The repo `TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin` is public with issues enabled. Kenneth chose a GitHub issue opened from a hidden tool that the model gets only when it is needed, over email and over an extra button on the existing report card.

Constraints:
- Read `AGENTS.md`, and `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any OrcaSlicer-owned file. Keep the change inside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` where possible.
- Build on a shared Mac: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, use `-j4`, and run one build per build directory.
- Temporary notes stay untracked.

Task:
Build a tool the JusPrin printer chat's model can call to open a pre-filled GitHub issue in the person's browser. The tool must be hidden from the model until it is needed: offer it only in a printer chat once the Bambu connection skill is in force, never in other chats or before that point.

What the tool does:
- It opens the person's default browser (`wxLaunchDefaultBrowser`, as `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp:311` and `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:125` already do) at `https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/issues/new` with `title` and `body` query parameters filled in.
- The model writes the title and a short summary: the printer model, what was tried, what the app reported, and what the person said. The app adds the app version and connection type.
- The person reviews it and presses Submit on GitHub themselves, so the app never posts anything. The tool result says the page was opened, not that an issue was filed.
- Keep the URL under about 8 KB; cut the body to fit and say so in the result. Never put the access code, API keys, the printer's serial (deviceId) or its IP address in the body. The existing connection report already hides deviceId; reuse that redaction if it fits.
- The model calls it only when the person agrees, as with every outward action. The tool description holds the rule about when to call it (the rule for one tool lives in that tool's description).

How it is offered:
- The skill is added by `PrinterConversation::connection_skill()` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:457`). That function returns the `connect_bambu` trigger once `m_connect_tried` is set, for a Bambu printer only. `AgentHost::session_skill()` (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1144`) attaches the skill to each request after that, and to the result of the tool call that set it (`AgentHost.cpp:2953` and `3131`).
- `AgentSkillUse` (`Agent/AgentService.hpp:51`) carries text only, so offering a tool from that point on is new code. Today every printer session is offered the same tools so the prompt cache holds (comment in `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool`). Adding this one tool after the skill fires costs one cache miss in those chats, which is accepted.
- Do NOT use hosted tool search, `defer_loading` or namespaced toolsets. Kenneth had that mechanism removed from the main line in October 2026; it lives on `feature/tool-deferral` and must not come back.
- It has to work for every provider the printer chat supports (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter/DeepSeek). Read `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` for how tools are added, and `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` for error codes.
- Mention the tool in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu/SKILL.md` only as knowledge, for example that a person stuck after trying can open an issue for the developers. Do not write a state-to-step table.

Done means:
- The tool is offered only after the connection skill is in force. Show this with a test: the tool list before and after the trigger, in `tests/agent` (agent_bridge_tests) or the shell harness.
- A test checks the URL it builds: encoding, the length cap, and no deviceId, IP or code in it.
- The existing AgentUI vitest suite and agent_bridge_tests pass. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` passes: the model reads "the app", never Orca.
- One check in the real app opens the browser at the pre-filled page, using the shell harness's printer chat with no live model if possible. No live-model run without Kenneth approving a specific batch and its cost.
- Commit on your own branch and report the commit. Do not push, merge or touch other branches.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 598f26fe-b466-4336-928e-14d10d45e1f7
  modified: 2026-09-08T16:33:59.964Z
---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

On 2026-10-08 a session running in `.claude/worktrees/<name>` tried to write a report next to its handoff in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/` and the Write tool was refused by a hook: edits to the base checkout "do not land on this session's branch and may corrupt the user's primary working copy". **Why:** handoffs are read from the main checkout ([[handoff-docs-not-committed]]), which makes it tempting to hand the report back in the same place.

**How to apply:** write reports and evidence folders in the worktree root, leave them untracked ([[temp-docs-stay-untracked-and-visible]]), and give Kenneth the worktree path. Never use the scratchpad for a deliverable; the app's file pane cannot open it as part of the project.

name: connection-skill-per-connection-type
description: "2026-11-02 Kenneth's chosen proposal for how the agent gets better printer knowledge over time: one connection skill per connection type, added when a person connects, driven by honest tool states, grown by reviewed PRs and opt-in reports. Recorded, not implemented."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 73de5d33-07b2-44a6-bbd2-bedca734a244
  modified: 2026-11-02T20:40:31.571Z
---

Kenneth confirmed this on 2026-11-02 (in a forked side session, "AI agent design for printer setup") as the one to try for the open problem in the P1S handoff: how the agent gets correct printer and connection knowledge when the team cannot test most printers.

Update, later on 2026-11-02: built for Bambu. "The one right next step for each" in point 2 below was a rewording, and the state-to-step table it produced failed on the real P1S. The skill now explains how the connection works: see [[connection-skill-explains-not-lookup]]. Print hosts have no skill yet, and the person-corrected-the-model report trigger is not built.

1. **When:** the moment a person tries to connect a printer in the chat, the app adds one skill to that conversation. Not before, and not for people who only pick a profile and prepare prints.
2. **What:** a text file in the repo, one per connection type (Bambu first, then Moonraker/OctoPrint), chosen by the app from the connection type, never by the model. It holds the procedure: which tool to call, what each reported state means, and the one right next step for each, including silence, where it tells the model to ask what the person sees and wait rather than conclude. It holds no menu wording the app cannot verify.
3. **Tools:** the status and connect tools report the situation exactly as the app observes it (heard nothing yet, port taken, plug-in missing, cloud mode, wrong code, the host's own refusal reason). The skill drives the conversation from those states; the tools never carry the procedure.
4. **Improvement loop:** the skill grows by pull request reviewed by a person, like OrcaSlicer's profiles. When the agent and the person are struggling, by a rule the app applies (a connect attempt failed twice, or the person corrected the model), the chat asks whether to send a report to the JusPrin developers. The person sees what will be sent and says yes or no; nothing is sent otherwise. The report holds the tool states and the connection turns, never the access code or API key, and goes to our server directly so people on their own API keys can send it too.
5. **Evidence rule:** before any skill line is written for a state, that state must have been made to happen for real. The Bambu side has mostly done this; the host side only for Moonraker and OctoPrint.

**Why:** it replaces three earlier ideas Kenneth rejected: steps in the standing prompt, a "file per printer model" that was invented jargon and the wrong key for Klipper hosts, and counting data points, which OrcaSlicer never does. Connection type is the key the code already has.

**How to apply:** when work on printer-connection guidance starts, build this, not a variant; check each state against [[p1s-connect-incident-2026-10-31]] and [[tool-result-states-method]] (Kenneth's test for what counts as a problem). Open as of 2026-11-02: Bambu plug-in code -1 on a wrong access code, never 5; whether -1 is a rejection or a timeout.

Kenneth chose the full contract (option a) for tool errors on 2026-10-21. Implemented as one commit, 29ae944fea, on branch `claude/tool-error-contract` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-error-contract`, cut from bed54fd8fe). Fast-forwarded onto `jusprin-newui` the same day and pushed. The branch and worktree were deleted after the merge; the follow-up 9ad6bb927f (workspace_inspect shows disabled copies) sits on top.

His answers to the five open decisions:
- D2: no `changed` or `next` fields in the error envelope. Messages carry the outcome.
- D3: one spelling of each code on both surfaces; MCP no longer renames codes.
- D4: a busy OrcaSlicer keeps failing (`busy`); the tool does not wait.
- D5: `local_save_failed` stays a failure even when the change ran.
- D6: report partial changes in the message (no rollback); prefer checking before changing.

**Why:** a code that means one next step, truthful about what changed, is what a model can act on; the old `unavailable_operation` → `workspace_unavailable` rename told MCP clients JusPrin was closed.

**How to apply:** a new failure picks a code from `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` (`fail()` throws on any other), and an "impossible" state throws instead of failing. Don't propose `changed`/`next` fields again. Background and inventory: the untracked `tool-error-reporting-sweep.md` in the main checkout. Related: [[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]], [[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].

description: "Reproduce any JusPrin tool behaviour without a live model in about 20 s per run: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py call(); two traps (leaked harness from `cd && cmd &`, slice_start on an unchanged sliced plate)"
metadata:

  originSessionId: 0b03c379-ea3d-491e-a0b3-9b5bf2a6240f

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

# Web search instead of the connection skill, 2026-11-02

I gave the printer chat Anthropic's `web_search` tool and left out the `connect-bambu` skill. Four live chats on the real P1S, with `claude-sonnet-5-5`, cost $0.11 in total. **The agent never searched once.** Every fact it gave came from its own knowledge, so these chats do not show whether search can supply what the skill knows.

## What I changed
The code is on branch `claude/connect-web-search`, uncommitted. All of it is test-only, behind environment variables:
- `JUSPRIN_TEST_WEB_SEARCH` adds the basic search tool (`web_search_20250305`, at most 5 searches a request) and keeps the skill out of the chat.
- The codec keeps search queries and citations when it sends a reply back.
- `JUSPRIN_TEST_HEAR_NOTHING` makes the app ignore the printers it hears, and a new `no-printer` scenario uses it.

The prompt, the tools and the app's notes are unchanged.

## The chats
Kenneth had restarted the printer, and it answered port 8883 in 10 to 123 ms. The skill's earlier chats ran while it was slow and got code -1, so they are not a like-for-like comparison.

| Chat | Requests | Searches | Wall time | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Normal connect | 4 | 0 | 42 s | $0.029 |
| Wrong code, twice | 8 | 0 | 65 s | $0.042 |
| Right code | 7 | 0 | 45 s | $0.012 |
| No printer heard | 7 | 0 | 150 s | $0.024 |

**Wrong code.** The app said "The printer refused the access code." The agent said: "My guess is a small typo, or the code on the printer has changed. Some printers show a new code after LAN mode is switched off and on." After the second refusal: "The code was refused a second time, so I don't think a typo is the cause. My new guess is that the printer I found isn't yours." It asked whether the screen shows 192.168.0.198. These are reasonable, labelled guesses with a cheap check.

**Right code.** It connected, and the agent said the person can close the chat.

**No printer heard.** First guess: off, other Wi-Fi, guest network or VPN. Told those were ruled out: "My next guess is that the printer isn't in LAN mode." **That is wrong:** a printer with LAN Only off is still heard, and the app reports it as in cloud mode. The skill says so, and the agent had no way to know. Told LAN Only is on, it moved to the firewall, AP isolation, or a mesh or extender. It never only waited, so the regression the skill caused (`connect-bambu-not-found`) did not appear.

## Problems
1. **No search ever ran.** The tool was offered: the cached prompt grew by the tool's 2,500 tokens. The model chose its own knowledge each time.
2. **A menu location stated as fact.** It told the person twice that the code is on the printer's screen "in its network settings" without calling it a guess. In the first chat it called the same claim a guess. I have not checked whether this is right for a P1S.
3. **The harness check misfires.** `live_p1s_words_do_not_say_no_printer` failed in three chats on the choice "I can't find it", which is about the code.

## Not tested
- A chat in which a search actually ran, so where the results come from and whether they are right for this printer.
- The 18 scripted suite cases, and a no-printer chat with the skill as a control.
- Failures on a slow printer, search with dynamic filtering, and showing sources to the person.

## Recommendation
Keep the skill. Search alone added nothing, because the model did not use it. The one fact the agent got wrong, LAN Only off is still heard, is how this app works, and a search would not find it. Search might still help with menus on printers the team has never tested. That needs a prompt line telling the model to look them up before guessing, which is Kenneth's call to approve and test.

# Guide for adding JusPrin tools

**Status:** This guide explains how to add a tool to JusPrin. The three things it builds on are already implemented: the shared tool registry, the MCP server embedded in the app, and the stdio bridge (a small helper program that connects external AI clients to that server). Over MCP, the tools currently cover inspecting the workspace, reporting on a slice for review, and the settings workflow. The settings workflow works on the process preset, on one object, and on filament and printer presets. Later in this guide there is a [candidate catalog](#candidate-catalog): a list of tools we might build, worked out from the product's screens. It follows the implemented catalog record. Nothing in the candidate catalog exists unless the catalog record says it does.

JusPrin has one tool system. A new capability is defined once, in the shared registry. `ToolExecutionCoordinator` runs it. Its implementation reads and changes the open project through the typed workspace interface. Two adapters, one for OpenAI and one for MCP, only translate that single definition into the format each side expects. The aim of this guide is a tool catalog that stays small, does only what it claims to do, can change safely over time, and is shaped by real printing tasks. It should not be shaped by a list of every feature OrcaSlicer has.

Treat this guide as the starting point. Change it when what you learn from implementing, from real MCP clients, or from evals shows that a rule, a contract, a limit, or a sequence here should change. Do not keep a planning assumption just because it is written here. Base every revision on evidence, and describe significant changes in the PR. Two things do not change: OrcaSlicer stays the owner of the state it owns, and the verification requirements stay.

Before you touch any OrcaSlicer class that holds live state, read [the production documentation](README.md), [production architecture](architecture.md), and [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md). The current tool definitions are in [`ToolRegistry.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp). The code that runs them is in [`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp). The code that presents them over MCP is in [`McpProtocol.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp).

External clients on the same machine connect through the bundled `jusprin-mcp` stdio helper, which is set up from **Connect AI tools...**. The helper and the server inside the app are compiled from the same registry. So every new tool you offer must have the same catalog entry and the same schema whether the app is running (live) or not (offline), for the same build and the same negotiated protocol version. Do not add a catalog that exists in only one adapter. Connecting to the server directly over HTTP is a route for developers. It is not what the default setup instructions tell people to do.

## Words this guide uses

- **Registry.** The one list of tool definitions, compiled into the app (`ToolRegistry.cpp`).
- **Catalog.** The list of tools as a caller sees it.
- **Coordinator.** `ToolExecutionCoordinator`, the class that queues tool calls and runs them on the GUI thread.
- **Workspace.** The typed C++ interface (`IWorkspace`) through which JusPrin reads and changes the open project. It has two implementations, called workspace adapters. The real one works on live OrcaSlicer. The fake one is for tests.
- **Tool adapter.** Code that translates registry definitions and results for one kind of caller. There are two: the in-app adapter, which uses OpenAI's format and serves the Agent panel, and the MCP adapter, which serves external clients. "Both adapters" in this guide means these two.
- **Projection.** The form in which one tool adapter presents a definition or a result.
- **Exposure.** The registry setting that says which callers are offered a tool.
- **Owner.** The OrcaSlicer class that holds the real copy of some state, or that already implements an operation.
- **Seam.** A small addition to a file OrcaSlicer owns, which lets fork code call or observe OrcaSlicer's behavior.

- **Eval.** An automated test that gives a model a task and checks the transcript that results.

## Current connection and execution boundary

- The server starts automatically with the JusPrin Agent panel. There is no `JUSPRIN_MCP` switch to enable it and no bearer token. The server listens only on the numeric loopback address. It prefers port 47301, and falls back to a port chosen by the operating system only when 47301 is taken.
- The shell tells the server where its discovery file is: `<data_dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`. The running server writes its details there in one atomic step: the actual address, the PID, a unique `instanceId` for this run, the build version, and the protocol versions. Before a server removes the record, it checks, while holding the discovery lock, that the record is its own. An older server therefore cannot remove a newer server's record, even inside the same process. On POSIX systems the file has mode `0600`.
- The helper checks that the discovery file is valid, and then tests that the address in it answers. When the app starts or restarts later, the helper follows the new record. The helper never launches JusPrin. The discovery file holds one record, and the last server to write it wins. So the helper works with one selected instance; there is no way to choose among several. `--discovery`, `JUSPRIN_MCP_DISCOVERY`, and `JUSPRIN_MCP_URL` override the file path or the address. They do not switch anything on. The connection entries that Connect writes use `--discovery` with the app's actual data directory.
- When the app is not running, the helper answers discovery and tool-list requests from the registry compiled into the helper. Tool calls made while the app is not running return `workspace_unavailable`. When the app can be reached, the helper uses the app's live catalog and results, even when the app and the helper are different versions. Do not replace a live app's tool list with the helper's compiled one. A version difference between the two is logged.
- The HTTP adapter accepts MCP protocol version `2026-07-28`. The helper can also negotiate the older versions `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18`, and `2025-11-25`. The helper does all conversion between versions. Code that executes a tool must not behave differently for different protocol versions.
- **Connect** shows the person the command or the file edit and asks for confirmation first. Then it either runs the Claude Code or Codex CLI, or merges the JusPrin entry into the JSON configuration of Claude Desktop/local Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. A JSON edit keeps unrelated settings and makes a backup. It is refused when the preview is out of date or when the destination is a symlink. It does not protect against another editor writing the same file at the exact moment of replacement.
- On macOS the helper is bundled next to the app executable. Windows has a matching install rule. On Linux, the entry for an AppImage uses the installed image's path plus `--mcp-bridge`, and the app handles that flag before the GUI starts. Do not save a temporary AppImage mount path as the command.

Workspace commands run on the GUI thread, through the shared coordinator. A timer owned by the shell keeps execution moving, so execution does not depend on the WebView's handshake. No external client ever gets direct access to OrcaSlicer objects.

A call from an external client is tagged `ToolSource::Mcp`. The MCP adapter sets that tag, so it can be trusted, and it is kept for the activity history and for diagnostics. External calls run through the same coordinator and the same workspace commands as calls from the in-app Agent. The change log records the edits they make, as it records every edit, and marks them `external`. In the conversation thread those edits appear as rows that say "External tool", where a change made in the app says "Agent".

## Start with an eval failure

The fact that OrcaSlicer has a menu item or a config key is not a reason to add a tool. Start from a transcript or an automated eval in which the Agent cannot finish a real user task, finishes it only some of the time, or needs an unreasonable number of steps or tokens.

Write down:

- what the user wanted to achieve;
- the exact point where the current tools stop being enough;
- which OrcaSlicer state or operation is missing;
- what a successful transcript should look like;
- the unsafe or ambiguous cases that must fail; and
- the evidence that will show the new tool fixed the problem.

If the failure can be fixed by a clearer description, a better result, or a more useful validation error, improve the existing definition instead of adding a tool.

The candidate catalog later in this guide lists tools we might build. Being listed there does not accept a tool, and it does not excuse a tool from this section. A row in that catalog does two jobs. It records which product screen and which group of evals the tool would serve, which makes the eval easier to write. ## Decide whether this should be a tool

Add or extend a tool when the Agent needs one of three things: up-to-date state read straight from OrcaSlicer, a calculation that OrcaSlicer does and that always gives the same answer for the same input, or a change to the live project.

Do not add a tool for:

- a single setting key. Setting keys are records that the generic settings tools search and edit;
- general printing advice that the model can work out from a skill;
- a fixed bundle of changes such as "make it stronger", where the right answer depends on the part and on what the user cares about;
- driving the UI, such as pressing a button or operating a widget or a hidden panel;
- data that an existing tool already returns in a size-limited result;
- a capability someone might want in the future, with no eval or user task behind it; or
- an operation that the real workspace adapter cannot truly perform through the OrcaSlicer class that owns it.

A fixed, mechanical step of a workflow can be a tool. Examples are generating OrcaSlicer's calibration geometry and starting OrcaSlicer's slice action. Advice should stay a skill until there is a separately specified operation behind it that always behaves the same way.

A skill is text the model reads. A tool is something the app executes. To decide which one a candidate is, ask one question: does it have to run, or does it only have to be read?

settings_search → settings_get → settings_preview_patch → settings_apply_patch

set_wall_loops
set_infill_density
set_support_angle

- preset selection, because OrcaSlicer may substitute a compatible preset, and dirty edits may be lost;
- topology changes such as cutting, splitting, or merging, because the caller needs to see the resulting pieces.

Sending a print is not a fourth. The agent opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog, which shows the person the slot mapping and the printer's readiness, and the person presses Send there (see [Sending a print](product-definition.md#29-sending-a-print)).

Everywhere else, the coordinator computes and validates the resulting state as part of the call. If a preview would only repeat its input back, do not make it a tool.

It gives way to the file-loaded skill on a request that carries both, since that skill already asks for the same check.
- `slice-failed` (trigger `slice_failed`): a plate's last slice did not succeed, because OrcaSlicer's check refused the plate or the run failed. The adapter records why on the plate (`WorkspacePlate::slice_failure`: refused or failed, OrcaSlicer's words, the setting and object when named) at the moment it happens (a hook in `Plater::reslice`, `Workspace/SliceRequests.hpp`, and the run's completion event), worded by the print-issue monitor's `slice_failure_of`, and keeps it until the plate slices. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceFailure`; `slice_report` of an unsliced plate adds the check code and the object's name. The skill fires once per failure, on the first request that carries it: the result of the model's own `slice_start`, the turn the app starts when a slice the model started fails after its turn, or the next message after the person's Slice all. The same refusal again is the same failure.
- `print-issues` (trigger `print_issues`): what the print-issue chip's Ask AI button asks for and how to read what OrcaSlicer reports. The adapter reads a slice's warnings through the monitor's `slice_warnings_of` while the plate is active and keeps a summary on the plate while that slice is current (`WorkspacePlate::slice_warnings`: the count, how many the person ignored, and the first warning, critical first, in OrcaSlicer's words with its setting and object). It counts every warning the chip lists. The chip and `slice_report` read the same slice-result rule (`Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`), so they list the same warnings, except that `slice_report` also lists the timelapse ones, marked `appliesWhen: "timelapse"`, which the chip does not count. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceWarnings`. The skill fires on the request that carries a chip's message, and on the first request whose workspace shows warnings no request has carried yet, whether the person sliced (their next message) or the model did (the tool result that shows them, or the app's turn when its slice ended after its turn); a re-slice with the same warnings fires nothing.

The cases in between:

- **A procedure made of existing tool calls.** It is a skill for as long as carrying it out takes judgement. It becomes a tool only when the steps are fixed and the person wants the whole thing as one action that can be undone. If there are many such fixed sequences, they go in one workflow registry (see [When resources or skills are appropriate](#when-resources-or-skills-are-appropriate)).
- **An analysis.** It is a tool when OrcaSlicer computes it and always gets the same answer, such as overhang angles from geometry. It is a skill when it is a judgement about evidence. Pair that skill with the tool that supplies the evidence (`view_render`, `slice_report`).
- **Large reference data.** When the model needs only one part of the data, make it a tool that returns the part an argument selects, as `settings_search` does. When the model needs to see all of the data before it can use any of it, make it text. The printer list described under [Input design](#input-design) is the case we measured: putting the whole list in the instructions worked better than the search tool.
- **A tool description versus a skill.** A tool description says when to call that one tool, in the words a person would use. A skill says how several tools fit together and what to conclude from their results. If a tool description has grown into a step-by-step procedure, move the procedure out into a skill.

When you are not sure, start with a skill. A skill is a text file that ships with the page. A tool costs the whole implementation sequence described below, including fakes, tests, and rebase evidence. Turn a skill into a tool only on the kind of evidence every tool starts from (see [Start with an eval failure](#start-with-an-eval-failure)). Either transcripts show the model getting the sequence wrong in ways that better text does not fix, or the action needs something only the app can give: all-or-nothing application, validation, or undo. The opposite sign exists too. If a skill has turned into exact values and calls in a fixed order, with no judgement between them, it should be written as a tool.

How something gets loaded into the model's context does not decide whether it is a skill or a tool. Today a skill costs its one line in the instructions, and a tool costs its definition on the first request of a conversation (see [Tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)). If we later use the model platform's deferred loading, both will cost one index line plus a load when needed. A skill could then be a deferred read-only tool: the tool's description is the skill's index line, and the tool's result is the skill's text. Tools and skills would then be found the same way and covered by the same eval.

## Tool budget and tool shape

The limit on the number of tools comes from how much the model has to load on each turn. It does not come from how much the app can do. The rules in this section rest on this evidence:

- OpenAI's function-calling guidance keeps fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn and defers the rest.
- Anthropic's [tool-writing guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents) asks for a few tools aimed at high-impact workflows. It names "tools that merely wrap existing software functionality or API endpoints" as the common error.
- A [domain-oriented MCP study](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22063v1) measured three interfaces. A generic interface of thin tools scored below raw SQL. Tools shaped around the domain scored far above both.
- The "god tool", one tool that dispatches many unrelated actions through a single `action` parameter, is a documented anti-pattern.

The current five-tool MCP catalog measures about 1.9 KB per definition, and two thirds of that is output schema.

**How tools are loaded for now.** Both adapters load every registered tool on every turn. The in-app adapter sends the full function list with each request, and MCP `tools/list` returns the whole catalog. This is the simplest behaviour that is correct. It also keeps the tools array byte-identical through a chat, and OpenAI's prompt cache depends on exactly that. The budget is 20 definitions per turn. Going over 20 does not block anything. It is the point at which we start watching the measurements. The live regression test records definition bytes, input tokens, and cached tokens for each request. The journey catalog below goes over 20 definitions from its first milestone. We accept that until those measurements show the model selecting wrong tools or running short of context.

**Deferral, when the measurements say so.** Deferral means the model first sees only a short index and loads a tool's full definition when it needs it. Use the deferral feature that the model platform provides. Never write our own mechanism for switching tools in and out. For the in-app Agent, the platform feature is OpenAI's `tool_search` with `defer_loading: true` on the Responses API. It is documented for `gpt-5.4` and later. Tools would be deferred one toolset at a time (toolsets are the named groups in the candidate catalog), and OpenAI recommends fewer than ten functions per namespace. Do not build a tool that enables a toolset by rewriting the tools array. Every switch would break the prompt cache.

**Shape each tool as a domain operation.** A tool does one thing that a slicer user has a name for: place an object, lay out the plates, mark a region, set up the printer. Do not wrap each OrcaSlicer function in its own tool. Do not build a tool that interprets a list of unrelated commands. One operation may have several optional facets, as long as each facet has its own type and the tool rejects facets that conflict.

**Batch only where items share a shape.** Good examples are a list of setting changes, a list of annotations, and a list of layout rows with one row per object. A list that mixes transforms, imports, and deletes is the god tool described above. It is refused.

**Fold reads into sections and detail levels before adding a read tool.** A new read tool is justified in only two cases. Either its inputs are of a different kind (a search over a large catalog, an analysis of one object, a report on a sliced plate), or its result is an image.

**Let call logs decide consolidation.** If transcripts show that two tools are always called together, consider merging them. If two facets of one tool are never used together, consider splitting them. Make these decisions from eval evidence, not from a design discussion.

**Output schemas are not advertised over MCP.** No client was shown to use them, and they were two thirds of the catalog. `tools/list` no longer carries `outputSchema`. `validate_output` still checks every successful MCP result, so a result that breaks its contract still fails with a visible error. We measured the effect on one build, with the recipe near the end of this guide. With five tools, the catalog went from 9,723 bytes to 3,141, which is from about 2,430 tokens to 785. Only the MCP side saves anything. The in-app adapter has always sent `input_schema` as `parameters` and nothing else, so an in-app turn never carried output schemas. Restore the field only for a client that is shown to read it.

## Choose the narrowest honest scope

Do not put an enum value in a schema, such as one of `printer | filament | process | object`, unless every advertised value works in both the fake and the real workspace adapter and inherits values the way the documentation says.
## Define the contract before the implementation

For every new tool, the registry entry, together with its contract and tests, must specify:

- a name that will not change, in lowercase with underscores;
- a short title, shown in the activity UI;
- a short description that says when to use the tool;
- a strict JSON Schema for the input, with `additionalProperties: false` where practical;
- a JSON Schema for the output;
- its `ActionClass`, which is trusted because it is set in the registry;
- whether it is offered to the in-app Agent, to MCP, or to both;
- what must be true for it to be available, such as an open FFF project (FFF is ordinary filament printing) or a selected object;
- whether the action is revision-sensitive, meaning it must fail when the workspace has changed since it was requested;
- whether it applies completely or not at all, and how it is really undone, reset, or reverted. Say so explicitly when normal project Undo does not apply;
- what happens when it is cancelled;
- the size limits on its output and how results are paged; and
- its errors, as structured codes that are specific to the task.

The registry cannot change while the app runs, and its entries always come in the same order. A tool adapter may leave tools out, based on the exposure each tool declares. An adapter must not change a tool's action class, validation, or behavior. Keep the list that MCP clients see stable. The only exception would be a server that also implements and tests the current protocol's notification for a changed tool list. When a tool cannot run because of the app's current state, report that from `tools/call` instead of removing the tool from the list.

`ToolDefinition` currently stores the name, title, description, input and output schemas, action class, exposure, availability, and handler. The other properties are not registry fields. Whether a tool is revision-sensitive, whether it is all-or-nothing, how it cancels, and how it appears in history are all determined by the coordinator and workspace code, and checked by their tests. `ToolAvailability` currently describes the session a tool is offered in (`Always`, or `SkillIndex` for `skill_read` when the page lists skills). It does not filter tools by the current state of the project or by what one message carries: on Anthropic the tools open every request, so a list that changes between requests of a chat voids that chat's whole prompt cache. `object_import` is offered on every turn, and a call that names no attached model file fails with `invalid_arguments`.

Inputs are validated by the `valid_arguments` decoder that the registry has for each handler. Changing only the JSON Schema does not change which calls are accepted. Successful MCP output is checked by `validate_output`, which deliberately understands only a small set of schema keywords. Before you use a keyword it does not support, extend the validator and add tests. Do not assume that `validate_output` implements all of JSON Schema, or that every adapter validates output automatically.

### Naming and compatibility

- Prefer names such as `slice_start` and `presets_compare`.
- Do not rename a released tool without a strong reason. Treat names and schemas as public APIs.
- Add optional fields in a way that keeps existing callers working. Do not change the meaning or the type of an existing field.
- When a breaking change to a contract cannot be avoided, add a versioned replacement. Stop advertising the old definition after a documented migration period, and keep a targeted compatibility test for as long as both exist.
- Use one canonical name for a tool in every adapter. Do not keep separate OpenAI and MCP aliases unless a defect in a client is documented and tested.

## Input design

A tool's inputs should say what the caller wants and which thing it wants it done to. They should not describe how the request is transported or how the UI works.

- Send OrcaSlicer IDs as JSON strings, so that the full width of the native ID is preserved.
- Use canonical setting keys, and values in their normalized form.
- The first catalog had three in-app fixtures: `duplicate_object`, `import_model`, and `inspect_selection`. All three are retired. `plate_layout` replaced the first, `object_import` replaced the second, and the selection ids in the summary of `workspace_inspect` replaced the third. When the coordinator queues an action, it records the session and the revision. It invalidates queued actions when a relevant workspace event arrives, and it checks again before executing. A change to the selection alone does not invalidate an action that is aimed at a specific object, and does not redirect it.
- Some new operations read a value, change it, and write it back, and must detect anything that changed since the caller's earlier read. For such an operation, design explicit inputs for the expected session and revision in its own schema and decoder, and test them. A check made when the call is submitted does not prove that the caller's earlier read is still current. Do not quietly add required arguments to tools that already exist.
- Put changes that must succeed or fail together into one call.
- Make the caller say which thing it means. Do not fall back to a hidden default. The exception is a tool whose name clearly promises the current selection or the active plate.
- Reject unknown fields. Reject inputs that select the target in conflicting ways.
- A caller may pass a filesystem path only to a tool that does three things: it validates the exact absolute path, it restricts what kind of file the path may be and where, and it documents whether it reads, creates, or overwrites. The candidate catalog has three such tools: `object_import_file`, `project_open`, and `export_file`. No read-only tool accepts a path. In-app clients keep using attachments, which need no path.
- Do not make the model repeat data that the server can read for itself, from the real source, when the call executes.
- Do not put a large catalog into a schema as an enum. Offer a size-limited search and a way to fetch details instead.

**One exception, with its evidence: the printer list.** Working out which printer someone means from what they say takes the model's understanding. It is not a lookup. A search tool placed in front of the model did the job badly. `printer_catalog_search` required every word of the query to appear in a model's name, and it returned the first few matches in file order. As a result "voron 2.4 350mm" came back unsupported, "x1c" matched another manufacturer's printer, and "prusa" showed three of thirteen.

So the instructions for an Add session now carry every printer the panel offers, one per line, in the form `<catalogId> | <brand> <model> | <build volume>`. There are 383 lines. They come from `PrinterCatalog::panel_printers`, are sent to the page as the session's `context`, and are written into the instructions by `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`. `printer_identify` checks the ids that the model copies from the list.

- the word test set: 138/150;
- the photo test set: 29/45;
- the handoff's own cases, with those four queries among them: 21/21.

The model tried 33 times to show more than three printers. Each attempt was refused with `too_many`, and the model then asked a question to narrow the choice. So no answer ever showed three of many. Two weak spots remain. One is a query that equals one model's name and is also the beginning of other models' names ("bambu a1": 0/3). The other is a photo with no readable name. The test sets and the runner are in `agent-docs/jusprin/spikes/printer-identify/`, which is uncommitted and sits beside the earlier spikes.

The list is always the same text at the start of the instructions, so it is cached. This approach is right only while the list stays at a few hundred lines.

The coordinator looks up the action class and the handler from the tool's name. Never accept either one from the call's arguments.

## Output design

Decide how large a response may be before you add fields to it. A full project tree, every setting definition, G-code statistics for every layer, or an unlimited list of warnings can each use more of the model's context than the entire tool catalog.

Every read tool should use one or more of:

- a level of detail (concise, default, or detail);
- explicit field selection;
- paging, with results always in the same order;
- a fixed maximum number of items;
- a summary first, followed by separate calls for the details the caller wants; or
- an explicit `truncated` flag and a cursor for fetching the rest.
